diagnosis.root_cause: Duplicate RADIUS radcheck rows for the same username, with conflicting line IDs. FreeRADIUS resolves the rows inconsistently, causing repeated authentication session disconnects and short-lived sessions.
evidence: The customer has 19 sessions in 24 hours, above the 8+ flapping threshold, and the average session duration is only 38 minutes versus the 11.9-hour network mean.
RX power is -20.62 dBm and TX power is 2.44 dBm, both within normal EPON ranges.
Optical telemetry is stable: RX variation is within the healthy noise range, TX variation is within the healthy noise range, distance is constant at 96, and TX bias remains healthy and flat.
The ONU is currently online and authenticated, and all tested peers on EPON0/5 are online with normal optics, ruling out an ONU, fibre, splitter, or shared PON fault.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, has normal CPU, memory, temperature, and all eight PONs are healthy; the router heartbeat and VLAN 1055 provisioning are also normal.
RADIUS contains two rows for the same username, one with the active CRM line ID and one orphan row with a conflicting line ID. This directly explains inconsistent authentication outcomes.

Because the physical layer is clean, the session count is at least 8, and the authentication defect is confined to duplicate rows on this customer, the presenting fault is session flapping caused by authentication data conflict.

remediation.action: Remove the orphan radcheck row containing line ID 1C:EF:03:90:2B:5A, retain and reconcile the active CRM line ID 00:A1:07:C4:1D:88, then clear stale sessions and verify stable reauthentication. Audit RADIUS uniqueness constraints and synchronization to prevent duplicate username rows.

ground_truth.root_cause: Two radcheck rows exist for the same username. FreeRADIUS resolves inconsistently between them, so authentication succeeds or fails depending on which row is matched, producing repeated short sessions and two alternating IP assignments.
expected_reasoning: 19 sessions in 24h against a 2-3 baseline, with a 38 minute mean duration against an 11.9 hour norm
RX has been flat at -20.6 dBm for seven days inside the +/-0.3 dBm noise floor, so signal is not the cause
TX power, bias current, supply voltage and distance are all stable
Port neighbours are normal and the OLT is healthy, so no shared infrastructure fault
With no optical explanation available, the search moves to the authentication layer
RADIUS holds two radcheck rows for username 30:16:9D:A2:5F:03, one of them an orphan with a different lineid
Recent sessions alternate between two IP addresses, consistent with inconsistent row resolution
Traffic is erratic rather than declining, which fits intermittent authentication rather than a degrading link

expected_escalation.review_reason: Duplicate RADIUS rows must be resolved by hand; deleting the wrong row disconnects the customer

distractors: The session pattern is identical to signal-related flapping and invites that diagnosis
Zero-throughput windows in the speed series look like link loss but coincide with rejected auth
ONU is a Router type, inviting a CPE-fault explanation
